$comment: Machine-readable acceptance thresholds (QUALITY_BAR section 5). Nothing in a test
hard-codes a number that also appears here, so relaxing one is a reviewable diff.
Each latency gate carries the release budget and, where a test asserts one, a
debugNNMilliseconds twin. Both are asserted: ViewerZoomGateTests picks the column that
matches the binary it is running in, and budgetsMatchTheThresholdFile fails the build if
this file and that test ever disagree. Before 2026-08-25 the timing budgets were asserted
in release only and no gate built release, so none of them was ever evaluated.
Scripts/verify-viewer-budgets.sh runs the suite optimised; build-app-package.sh
asserts the debug column.
This file was created with the viewer gates Z1-Z10 of QUALITY_BAR section 6. The C1, C2
and C3 thresholds of sections 2, 3 and 4 are not yet transcribed into it; until they are,
the rule above holds for the viewer and automation budgets only. That is a stated gap, not a claim.
Latency budgets below retain their recorded values; reference-machine details are omitted.
The unspecified strings and memoryGB value 0 denote omitted metadata, not hardware values.
oldestSupportedHardwareAllowance remains the explicit allowance for older supported hardware
until measured. The allowance is stated, never folded into the number.

viewer.$fixture: Synthetic Roof Plan (ZPDFTestingSupport synthetic-roof-plan/1, generated by the test suite, the same bytes on every machine; Packages/ZPDFTestingSupport/FIXTURES.md), 1 page, A1 landscape, crop 2383.94 x 1683.78 pt, 16 341 extracted primitives
viewer.$viewportModel: 1600 x 1000 view points at backing scale 2 = 3200 x 2000 device pixels

Z1.gate: Main-thread work per frame while zooming or panning, page presentation only, markups excluded
Z1.derivation: A pixel-exact viewport blit is 1.71 ms p50 and the vector underlay adds 0.38 ms p50 CPU (historical benchmark). 4 ms leaves 12.6 ms of a 16.6 ms frame for markups.
Z1.debugDerivation: Worst debug p50 ever measured 0.853 ms; twice that, rounded up, is 2 ms, which is also the release budget, and a debug budget is never tighter than the release one. The blit is CoreGraphics work, optimised in both configurations: 0.519-0.853 ms debug against 0.537-0.547 ms release on the same machine.

Z2.gate: Frames missed during a sustained fit to 400 % pinch of 36 steps, and no rasterisation on the main actor

Z3.gate: Time from a zoom settling to a fully sharp viewport, page already parsed
Z3.sampleShape: 3 blocks of 40 warm renders per zoom, pooled. The gate asserts the pooled p50 and the pooled p95 and prints min, p50, p95, max and the three block medians at every zoom, so the distribution is in the log rather than in somebody's memory.
Z3.derivation: RESTATED 2026-08-25 from a measured distribution, replacing 12.0 ms. The 12.0 came from one line of the historical benchmark (warm rasters 4.3 to 11.1 ms p50, rounded up) and sat inside the measurement's own spread. Over 24 consecutive release runs of the same binary on the reference machine, load average 4.8 to 5.7 throughout and correlation between load and result -0.04, the worst-zoom warm p50 was min 10.349, p50 11.295, p95 13.143, max 13.186, sd 0.886; SEVEN OF THE TWENTY-FOUR missed 12.0. 4800 individual warm samples (20 runs x 6 blocks of 40 at zoom 1.00) split that spread almost evenly: between-run sd 0.775, mean within-run block-to-block sd 0.687, so about half of it was draw noise that more samples in one run remove. The gate therefore pools 3 blocks of 40 (sd 0.959, worst of 40 observations 14.330) and the budget is derived by a stated rule: above the highest value the pooled statistic has ever produced on this machine, plus at least one further standard deviation, rounded up. 14.330 + 0.959 = 15.289, so 16.0 ms. It is still inside one 60 Hz frame period of 16.67 ms, which is the sentence Z3 exists to guarantee, and it fires on a 43 % regression of the measured 11.2 ms median. Verified over 48 further runs of the pooled shape (24 isolated, 24 whole-suite): min 9.559, max 12.723, zero over budget. One measurement worse than 14.330 has ever been recorded - 15.952, from the first end-to-end gate run after the restatement - and it was traced to the gate measuring seconds after its own ~90 s all-core release compile, the same fingerprint as the first miss ever recorded for Z3. verify-viewer-budgets.sh now waits after the build until the one-minute load average is back under the five-minute one (floor 10 s, ceiling ZENIT_VIEWER_BUDGET_COOLDOWN_SECONDS, default 120), which was verified against a deliberate 75 s CPU-load burst: it waited 93 s from a load average of 37.4 and then measured 10.702. The budget was not adjusted after that scare; the cause was removed instead, and 16.0 covers even the un-settled 15.952.
Z3.debugDerivation: Worst debug figures across sixteen debug runs (three full-suite runs of 2026-08-25, ten isolated runs of 2026-08-25 and the three build-app-package.sh runs that verified the fix): p50 14.273 ms, p95 32.448 ms. Twice each, rounded up, is 29 ms and 65 ms. The p95 ranged 12.133 to 32.448 ms across those runs, a 2.7x spread on an idle machine, so the doubling is the conservative reading of a two-sample-wide percentile. The debug column was derived under the noisier one-block shape and stays there: the pooled shape the gate now uses is strictly less noisy, so a debug budget derived from the old one cannot be too tight, and tightening a configuration this pass did not re-measure twenty times over would repeat the original mistake in the other direction.

Z4.gate: Same, for the first viewport of a page whose content stream has not been parsed
Z4.derivation: Cold viewport rasters 27 to 31 ms p50, 34 to 154 ms p95; the content-stream parse alone is about 19 ms (historical benchmark).
Z4.debugDerivation: Worst debug cold ever measured 40.7 ms; twice that, rounded up, is 82 ms, which is inside the 120 ms release budget, and a debug budget is never tighter than the release one, so it stays at 120 ms.

Z5.gate: Sharpness. Magnification of the displayed raster once the viewport has settled
Z5.derivation: Historical benchmark: the 24 MP whole-page cap stopped the canvas re-rendering above 122 % zoom.

Z6.gate: Pixel alignment. Every raster destination rectangle, in device pixels
Z6.derivation: Historical benchmark: 0.04 of a pixel costs 7.1x to 7.5x.

Z7.gate: Memory, hard-enforced, not hoped for. Steady state per open document
$comment: The 32 MiB viewport clause is a budget on the reference 1600 x 1000 pt window at
backing scale 2, where a raster with the 64 pt overscan margin is 3456 x 2256 =
29.7 MiB. It is enforced in ViewportRasterPlanner, in a stated order: a plan over the
ceiling loses its overscan margin first, and only a bare viewport still over budget is
refused. Sharpness is never the thing traded away. On a larger display the raster is
larger, and the invariant that holds everywhere is the one that matters: a viewport
raster is bounded by the window and never by the sheet.
The tile cache clause is not yet enforced anywhere: tiles are not built.

Z8.gate: Whole-page rasterisation above the pixel budget is forbidden, not clamped

Z9.gate: Cancellation grain: work already committed when a render is superseded
$comment: The grain today is one viewport render, 2.8 to 11.2 ms warm on the reference machine.
A 1.0 ms grain needs the 512 x 512 tile step, which is not built. Recorded as an open
gap rather than asserted, per QUALITY_BAR section 5: a gate nobody can meet is
reported as blocked, not passed.

Z10.derivation: Historical benchmark: the Core Graphics backend needs 98.6 to 134.3 ms per frame at 100 % and fit. Shipping a 7 fps underlay would be worse than shipping none.

Z11.gate: Main-thread time per gesture frame: the zoom input plus the display tick, plus the page-view draw the frame requires. A 72-step pinch fit to 800 % and back plus six 12-step gestures, replayed at 120 Hz on the benchmark sheet, pages 1 and 2 bare and page 1 with 500 captioned areas
Z11.derivation: NL-PERF-01: a 120 Hz frame is 8.33 ms; 4 ms p99 leaves half of it to the render server. This finally enforces Z1's p99 clause on the displayed gesture frames, which Z1's settled blit never did.
Z11.debugDerivation: Debug column: twice the worst of three quiet debug runs of the fixed canvas (2026-09-23, load < 25), rounded up, never tighter than release. Z11 p99 worst 2.32 -> 5; Z13 p50 94 -> 190, p95 207 -> 420; Z14 p99 4.19 -> 9. Release measured 2026-09-23 on the fixed canvas: Z11 p50 0.294 p99 1.931, Z12 0, Z13 p50 44.8 p95 87.4, Z14 p99 1.826. Before the fix (release): Z11 p99 24.996, Z12 409 of 432 frames blank, Z13 p50 84.5, Z14 p99 23.074.

Z12.gate: Blank-paper frames: gesture frames on which rasters cover less than 99.9 % of the visible sheet
Z12.derivation: A blank flash reads as stutter even when the frame rate is fine. Zero is the only honest number.
Z12.debugDerivation: Debug column: twice the worst of three quiet debug runs of the fixed canvas (2026-09-23, load < 25), rounded up, never tighter than release. Z11 p99 worst 2.32 -> 5; Z13 p50 94 -> 190, p95 207 -> 420; Z14 p99 4.19 -> 9. Release measured 2026-09-23 on the fixed canvas: Z11 p50 0.294 p99 1.931, Z12 0, Z13 p50 44.8 p95 87.4, Z14 p99 1.826. Before the fix (release): Z11 p99 24.996, Z12 409 of 432 frames blank, Z13 p50 84.5, Z14 p99 23.074.

Z13.gate: Gesture end to a fully sharp viewport (every visible pixel from a raster made for the final zoom, placed 1:1), any debounce included
Z13.derivation: Professional viewers sharpen within about a tenth of a second of the fingers stopping.
Z13.debugDerivation: Debug column: twice the worst of three quiet debug runs of the fixed canvas (2026-09-23, load < 25), rounded up, never tighter than release. Z11 p99 worst 2.32 -> 5; Z13 p50 94 -> 190, p95 207 -> 420; Z14 p99 4.19 -> 9. Release measured 2026-09-23 on the fixed canvas: Z11 p50 0.294 p99 1.931, Z12 0, Z13 p50 44.8 p95 87.4, Z14 p99 1.826. Before the fix (release): Z11 p99 24.996, Z12 409 of 432 frames blank, Z13 p50 84.5, Z14 p99 23.074.

Z14.gate: Main-thread work when a render lands, plus the page-view redraw the landing causes
Z14.derivation: NL-PERF-03: the end of every gesture had a visible hitch from slicing, copying and a full redraw on the main actor.
Z14.debugDerivation: Debug column: twice the worst of three quiet debug runs of the fixed canvas (2026-09-23, load < 25), rounded up, never tighter than release. Z11 p99 worst 2.32 -> 5; Z13 p50 94 -> 190, p95 207 -> 420; Z14 p99 4.19 -> 9. Release measured 2026-09-23 on the fixed canvas: Z11 p50 0.294 p99 1.931, Z12 0, Z13 p50 44.8 p95 87.4, Z14 p99 1.826. Before the fix (release): Z11 p99 24.996, Z12 409 of 432 frames blank, Z13 p50 84.5, Z14 p99 23.074.

Z15.gate: Main-thread time per pointer frame, one budget pair per replay: the page view's mouseMoved handler (loupe, hover scan over rotation knobs, vertex handles and markups, link hover, cursor readout, snap request) plus the observation refresh it triggers, plus the page-view, live-overlay and loupe-lens redraw the frame requires, plus the snap landing (the live-lane refresh and the redraw it causes) when it lands before the next frame. 240 moves at 120 Hz over 400 markups on the A4 fixture with the snap settings a new project starts with, twice: Select with a text box selected, and Length with the loupe on
Z15.derivation: U-005, 2026-09-27. Release: 1.5 x the worst of eight release runs on a settled machine (load average 2.7-3.2, Scripts/verify-viewer-budgets.sh's build flags: -c release -enable-testing -DZPDF_MOCKS, filtered to z15_pointerReplay), rounded up to the next 0.5 ms. Select: p50 1.144-1.478 -> 2.5, p99 2.580-2.890 -> 4.5. Length with the loupe: p50 1.754-1.954 -> 3.0, p99 2.159-4.071 -> 6.5. Every p99 budget stays inside one 120 Hz frame (8.33 ms). The two replays are budgeted apart because pooling them put the p50 between two populations: the first version's pooled p50 swung from 1.07 to 2.29 ms between release runs of one binary and hid the loupe behind the Select frames. Before these budgets were set the loupe was made cheaper: the crop is taken at backing resolution (it was magnified 4x on the CPU into 264 x 264 px, which CoreGraphics resampled bilinearly at every interpolation quality) and handed straight to a layer that SwiftUI never sees, and the lens is measured once per caption shape instead of every move; with default snapping the loupe replay's p50 went from 3.16-3.41 ms (SwiftUI Image of each crop) to 1.75-1.95 ms. What remains is SwiftUI's update of the lens caption and snap chip (lens commit p50 1.38-1.50 ms). Load sensitivity, measured and not budgeted: with 16 CPU-bound processes running (load 6.6-10.8, four runs) Select stayed at p50 1.10-1.23 / p99 1.80-2.62, while the loupe went to p50 3.41-3.79 / p99 5.35-10.01, because the lens commit waits on SwiftUI and Core Animation work a busy machine starves. The gate's cool-down waits out its own build; a red loupe line on a busy machine is re-run alone before it is read.
Z15.debugDerivation: Debug column: twice the worst of three quiet debug runs (2026-09-27, load average 1.5-2.0, the final canvas), rounded up, never tighter than release. Select p50 1.381 / 1.499 / 1.577 -> 4, p99 3.350 / 2.935 / 2.955 -> 7; Length with the loupe p50 2.352 / 2.650 / 2.802 -> 6, p99 2.917 / 4.067 / 3.781 -> 9. Five earlier debug runs at load 7.7-10.5, with concurrent background browser workloads, fit inside the column in four (Select p50 <= 1.736, p99 <= 3.245; loupe p50 <= 2.841, p99 <= 4.695); the fifth measured the loupe at p50 4.184 and p99 17.659 ms, which no honest debug budget covers. Layouts 0 and scene fetches 0 in every run, release and debug, and a snap landed within the frame on 227-240 of 240 Select moves and 54-240 of 240 loupe moves.

automation.$source: NL-AUTO-25; asserted by AutomationBenchmarkTests (ZPDFAppCore), run by Scripts/automation-benchmark.sh
$comment: Precision and recall per detector over a labelled corpus. The synthetic corpus
(ZPDFTestingSupport AutomationSyntheticCorpus) always runs; the optional real-drawing corpus run
when ZENIT_AUTOMATION_CORPUS names their manifest, against the same gates.
Symbols: a found position within the label's matchRadius of a labelled instance.
Rooms: a traced or closure-proposed area within 0.10 % of the labelled area (QUALITY_BAR).
Sheet names and scales: exact text of the sheet number and of the ratio.
